correctness.rationale: The standard unordered cubical deleted-product model is a deformation retract for this finite simple graph. Reconstructed chain ranks are (496,1440,1032), all signed consecutive boundaries vanish, and exact rank over F_101 is 928. All 186 enumerated disjoint short-cycle tori are integral 2-cycles. A deterministic 104-square-coordinate projection has column HNF exactly I_104, giving 104 independent cycles and hence ker(d2) of rank exactly 104. Projection is an integral isomorphism on the kernel, proving all 186 tori generate. Exact Smith normal forms: 72 six-six columns have 72 unit factors; the 168 columns with a hexagon have 102 unit factors and two factors 2; all 186 generate. Graph isomorphism enumeration gives precisely 192 automorphisms and orbit sizes 24,48,96,6,12; HNF proves each of the two octagon-pair orbits separately completes generation. Source checker verify_dyck.py reconstructs every requisite integer matrix from the LCF graph, without external numerical data.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An ordered-space Betti-number formula, even if applicable, cannot imply index-four structure inside the integral lattice of the unordered space. The planar toric generation theorem does not apply to this nonplanar graph; nor does it distinguish 6-cycle versus 8-cycle generator sublattices. A general generation claim would not imply the intermediate Smith factors or the two separate orbit completions.

value.rationale: The 32-vertex Dyck graph has two geometrically canonical regular-map structures, with 16 hexagonal faces in its toroidal realization and 12 octagonal faces in its genus-three realization. Disjoint cycle-pair tori of precisely these naturally distinguished face lengths ask which embedding geometry supplies integral second-homology generators. The exact intermediate index-four quotient (Z/2)^2 is invisible rationally, and the separate six- and twelve-element octagon-pair orbits each provide a sharp two-generator completion. This is a complete, motivated lattice invariant with a concrete structural explanation and does not follow from knowing the Betti number alone.
